steps.what: Observe plant and animal species and collect the specimens or images needed to study their structure and behavior.
Record the observed traits, location and specimen identifiers in the field notebook draft as each observation is made.
outputs: Field notebook draft in biological recording software

steps.what: Find the relevant taxonomic key and reference descriptions for the observed species traits using the reference library {DOCS}.
Identify and classify the organisms, comparing uncertain traits with the specimens and checking the final notebook identification against the evidence.
outputs: Evidence-qualified identification and checked final notebook version

steps.what: Save that checked identification and its observation record in the biological recording software {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure indexed reference collections and existing field-record forms. Retrieval can reduce finding pages; it cannot establish species identity from incomplete observations. Keep fieldwork, actual capture and classification with the biologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant keys are dispersed across the biologist's existing reference collection.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference-library search and taxon filters can narrow the pages to inspect.
tasks.still_hard: Overlapping traits, seasonal changes and uncertain specimens.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which observations distinguish the organism and preserving uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Field and taxonomic judgment remain central.

evidence.claim: Indexed taxonomic references can reduce lookup work without determining the identification.

assumptions: Illustrative active-work allocation, not a measured baseline; lookup saving applies only to repeated manual searches in an existing reference collection.
s1 and s2 alternate during field observation. Capture is real work, not a free clean dataset. No field upload or publication is assumed.
s4 is the ordinary completed-record check, not an extra self-approval stage. a1 binds its exact final version; edits require another check. Save time remains fully retained.
research_questions: Does an observation sample show repeated searches that saved filters would shorten?

already_counted.description: Fieldwork, capture, reference inspection, taxonomic judgment and save remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain reference tags and check outdated key links.

approvals.approved_version: Exact identification and observation record checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 10 x 30% lookup reduction = 3 gross points; less 0.5 upkeep. Existing indexed lookup yields zero. Estimates are E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study principles of plant and animal life

steps.what: Study plant and animal life through direct examination and observation relevant to the origin, development or function question.
Write the observed developmental or functional evidence in the research notebook draft {DOCS}.
Find and inspect existing research on the specific anatomy, relationship or function question using the scholarly reference manager {OTHER}.
outputs: Relevant sources with inspected methods and limitations

steps.what: Develop and challenge the biological explanation, write its limitations in the notebook {DOCS}, and check the final argument against the observations and sources.
Save the checked research notebook version {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Use saved scholarly searches and duplicate filtering before adding any model. They shorten finding relevant sources; critical reading and biological reasoning remain human. Actual observations must still be produced and recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated broad searches return already-read references.
tasks.enabler_now: A reference manager can retain searches and reading history.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing causal mechanisms from plausible stories.
tasks.human_edge: Designing observations and revising explanations when evidence conflicts.
tasks.altitude: The biologist remains responsible for the explanation.

evidence.claim: Saved scholarly searches and duplicate filters can reduce repeat retrieval, while source appraisal remains human.

assumptions: This is a separate basic-principles inquiry, not a second saving on the species-identification episode in task 178.
The 15% source step includes real reading; only repeated retrieval is reduced. Active-work shares are hypotheses, not organisational measurements.
Observation and capture alternate. s4 already writes and checks the final explanation. Its exact version gates the fully retained save without an added self-approval ceremony.
unknowns: Time spent on new reading versus finding sources
research_questions: Which recurring searches could be saved without narrowing the evidence too early?

already_counted.description: Direct study, observation capture, source appraisal and scientific reasoning remain counted.

incremental.description: Refresh saved queries and remove irrelevant alerts.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final research explanation checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 15 x 20% = 3 gross points, less 0.5 query upkeep. Already effective searches give zero. No experimental or reasoning saving claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect and analyze ecological relationship data

steps.what: Collect biological data about organisms and their environment through the planned field observations and measurements.
Enter the observed values, identifiers and measurement caveats into the ecological data workbook {SPREADSHEET}.
outputs: Populated raw observations with missingness and units

steps.what: Inspect missing observations, unit differences and sampling anomalies and decide the valid analysis dataset {SPREADSHEET}.
Set up repeated group summaries and relationship plots of the qualified biological data in {SPREADSHEET}.
Interpret organism-environment relationships, write the biological conclusions {DOCS}, and check the final dataset and plots against source measurements.
outputs: Checked final analysis and ecological interpretation

steps.what: Save the checked data and analysis version in the study folder {DOCS}.
inputs: Final dataset and analysis checked in s5

tasks.design: Configure native workbook query, grouping and plot refresh for repeated analyses. Keep actual field capture, cleaning decisions and ecological interpretation. No new model is needed for the calculations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated manual selection of ranges and rebuilding the same summaries.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing spreadsheet query and chart configuration can retain an inspectable analysis recipe.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing ecological meaning and defensible exclusions.

evidence.claim: Configured spreadsheet transformations and plots can reduce repeated active setup for stable study schemas.

assumptions: Conditional example where s4 is repeated manually today; the share is an E1 planning allocation, not a measured baseline. Existing automatic refresh has no saving.
Collection and entry alternate. Source values are produced in s1 and captured in s2; no clean dataset is assumed. No extra import saving is claimed.

s5 supplies the ordinary completed-analysis check for the exact-version save gate. Save effort is retained fully; any edit invalidates that check. This episode is not counted again under species classification or basic research.
research_questions: Can one retained recipe reproduce prior plots including missing-data cases?

already_counted.description: Field collection, actual entry, qualification, residual setup and final interpretation/check remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain the recipe when units or sampling schemas change.

approvals.approved_version: Exact dataset, plots and interpretation checked in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 15 x 50% setup reduction = 7.5 gross points minus 1 recipe upkeep. No existing calculation runtime counted as human saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assemble the actual reports and proposals to review, their map versions, supporting surveys and applicable policy sources in {DOCS}.
outputs: Versioned review source set with missing items identified

steps.what: Locate each required subject and its supporting passage in the proposal, building a review evidence matrix {DOCS}.
outputs: Draft source-linked evidence matrix including absent evidence

loop.purpose: Locate evidence for a fixed review checklist
loop.input: Versioned supplied reports and selected checklist
loop.output: Draft matrix with source page and quoted evidence or explicit not found
loop.check: Biologist verifies every material mapping against the original page and keeps conflicting evidence
loop.stop: At most two drafts; inaccessible pages, conflicts or unsupported items go to manual review
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native text search and required-field rules first; a bounded model helps map varied narrative wording to checklist subjects

steps.what: Judge the reports' accuracy and adequacy and adherence to the applicable policies and scientific standards, reading the original evidence and resolving material gaps.
outputs: Human scientific review findings with unresolved limitations

steps.what: Write the actual review findings and conditions in {DOCS} and check the final review, proposal version and intended recipients before release.
outputs: Checked final review package and recipient list

steps.what: Save the checked review package {DOCS}.
Send the exact checked review to the responsible planning recipient through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Start with document indexing and required-subject checks. Add a bounded source-linked extraction loop for narrative proposals. It locates evidence; the biologist makes every adequacy or compliance judgment and writes the final review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is spread through long reports with inconsistent section names.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked extraction can organise supplied evidence into a fixed review matrix.
tasks.still_hard: Ecological sufficiency, contradictory surveys and which standards apply.
tasks.human_edge: Determining whether evidence supports the development proposal.

ambition.what: Improve traceability of the existing review.

evidence.claim: A bounded document model can help locate candidate evidence in supplied reports, subject to full material source checks.

assumptions: The workload split is an unmeasured E1 scenario; the gain concerns actual evidence-location work, not an invented report-writing baseline.
The source set and checklist are produced or selected by the biologist in s1. Existing sources only; absent surveys are not fabricated or treated as complete.

s4 is ordinary final review production and checking. It gates the exact saved and sent version without added self-approval work; edits or recipient changes require recheck. Saving and sending each retain 1%.
This is scientific advice within existing authority, not the planning authority's permission to develop land. Other reviewers' decision labour is outside the saving.
unknowns: Share of time genuinely spent locating evidence
research_questions: Does a blind sample preserve contradictory evidence and correctly mark missing topics?

already_counted.description: Source assembly, residual matrix review, full scientific judgment, final writing/checking and actions remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain checklist mappings and inspect extraction failures after source-format changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final review package checked in s4
Exact review package and recipients checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 25 x 40% evidence-location reduction = 10 gross points minus 2 maintenance. Judgment, final prose, save and send have no claimed saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Biological observation, interpretation and scientific accountability remain with the biologist.
role.ambitious_version: A biologist who spends less time finding sources and rebuilding summaries while preserving fieldwork and scientific judgment.
